'''''Impatiens sodenii''''' is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Balsaminaceae]] known by the common names '''poor man's rhododendron''',<ref name=sf>Nickel, E. [http://www.sfgate.com/homeandgarden/pickoftheweek/article/Impatiens-sodenii-the-ideal-shrub-for-shady-spots-2374755.php ''Impatiens sodenii'' the ideal shrub for shady spots.] ''San Francisco Chronicle'' April 15, 2011.</ref> '''Oliver's touch-me-not''',<ref name=usda>[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=IMSO ''Impatiens sodenii''.] USDA PLANTS.</ref> and '''shrub balsam'''.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 29 January 2018}}</ref> It is native to [[Kenya]] and [[Tanzania]],<ref name=grin/> and widely cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]].

==Description==
This plant is a [[subshrub]] growing up to 2.5 meters tall. The stems are [[Succulent plant|succulent]], and woody toward the bases. It is hairless, with leaves in whorls of up to 12, especially near the ends of the branches. The leaves are widely lance-shaped, or occasionally more oblong, with toothed edges. They are up to 18 centimeters long. 

Flowers occur year-round, singly or in pairs. They are pink, but white forms, sometimes with darker markings are found. Petals measure 5-6 centimeters (2 to 2.4 inches), but horticultural forms may be as large as 14 cm. (5.5 inches) in width. The lowest [[sepal]] behind the corolla tapers into a long, thin spur up to 8 centimeters long. The greenish fruit capsule is up to 2.4 centimeters long and undergoes [[explosive dehiscence]] when mature.<ref name=iewf>[http://www.iewf.org/weedid/Impatiens_sodenii.htm ''Impatiens sodenii''.] International Environmental Weed Foundation (IEWF).</ref>

==Cultivation==

This plant is used as an ornamental garden shrub, and is of easy cultivation in moderate climates. Once established it is moderately drought tolerant, but will flower more freely if watered consistently. It is tolerant of light frost. 
Propagation may be from cuttings, or from seed, if the seed can be caught. 

It is a recipient of the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/9155/Impatiens-sodenii/Details | title = ''Imaptiens sodenii'' | website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 21 September 2020}}</ref>

Several [[cultivar]]s have been selected or bred, including the very large white-flowered 'Madonna', 'Flash' with white flowers with pink markings, and 'La Vida Rosa' which has flowers marked with a deeper pink.<ref name=sf/>

===Weed===
This is the most commonly grown impatiens in [[New Zealand]], where it has [[escaped plant|escaped cultivation]] and become a [[weed]].<ref name=bop>[https://www.weedbusters.org.nz/what-are-weeds/weed-list/shrub-balsam/ Shrub balsam.] Bay of Plenty Regional Council.</ref> It is cultivated in [[Australia]], where it has [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalized]] in a few areas in [[Western Australia]] and [[New South Wales]].<ref name=iewf/> It is documented as an [[introduced species]] in the [[Canary Islands]], [[Hawaii]], and [[Colombia]].<ref name=grin/>
